# Test kit model status

<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @synthetos/testkit gen:status` from src/honesty/behaviours.ts. Do not edit. -->

DEV ONLY. The firmware models in this package exist for tests; they never ship (RUN_PLAN §8.1, T-S40).
Every behaviour a safety claim depends on carries a citation at a pinned commit and a status
(RUN_PLAN §8.1 honesty rule). Pins: EN = TinyG edge-next `a7489b79`, TG = master `d0418390` (440.21),
EN-HIL = edge-next `tests/hil/`; EN3 = step-3 source `c7f9b7e2` (`vendor/firmware-pins.json`).
EN45004 = research source `ee98f02b545f3548fe53e59d143715141cfaf510`, not a vendor pin or build approval.
EN45004, EN, EN3 and TG paths are under `firmware/tinyg/`. EN3 is an optional model capability, not a build approval.

Totals: 99 behaviours (4 UNVERIFIED, 95 verified-source, 0 verified-bench).

## UNVERIFIED (release checklist)

Each must be bench-verified, or covered by a mitigation that does not depend on it, before the phase that relies on it ships.

| Id | Status | Behaviour | Citation | Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EN-EEPROM-STALL | UNVERIFIED | A persisted SET that changes EEPROM stalls the board while the bytes are written: input received meanwhile is lost and the answer goes out when the write ends. Off by default in the model (eepromWriteMs); the duration is a model value. | EN persistence.c:93-101 | B-EEPROM-1 (proposed: time a persisted write and send a GET during it; firmware maintainer note 2026-11-02) |
| TG-HARD-ALARM-SPINDLE | UNVERIFIED | The hard alarm's spindle off is itself a queued command behind a stopped runtime; the model keeps the spindle on (the conservative reading). Whether it actually turns off is not known. | TG canonical_machine.c:603-604; TG spindle.c:91-96 | B-TG-ALARM-1 (proposed; not yet in PROTOCOL_NOTES §15) |
| TG-OVERRUN-SPLICE | UNVERIFIED | After an overrun the reader joins the head of one line to the tail of another, and the spliced line runs if it parses. (E162) | TG xio/xio_usb.c:186-191 | B-FC-1 |
| TG-PROGRAM-END-SPINDLE | UNVERIFIED | At program end the finalize queues spindle off and coolant off as further commands; the model runs them in queue order. | TG canonical_machine.c:1363-1371 | B-M2-1 |

| EN-INHIBITED-JOINT | verified-source | Motor space: each executed segment sets the step target to the joint of its ABSOLUTE target and moves the motor by the difference from the previous step target; the joint of an INHIBITED axis is 0 (the live axis mode, read on every segment). So an axis inhibited while its motor is away from step 0 is driven to step 0 by the first segment of the next move of any axis, and an axis un-inhibited while its position is away from 0 is driven out to it, while the reported position shows neither. A step resync (cm_set_position, from a queue flush, and G28.3) rewrites the step targets from the position and moves nothing. ## Model limits

Simplifications of the models. No safety claim may rest on them.

| Id | Scope | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| LIM-KINEMATICS | both | Moves run at cruise speed with no acceleration ramps; a feedhold decelerates linearly over a fixed time (holdDecelMs, default 100 ms). Positions and durations are coarse. |
| LIM-ARCS | both | Arcs only in G17 with incremental I/J; one planner block per arc (EN queues arc segments from a callback); the end position is the commanded target, not the last computed segment. R-format, G18/G19, G90.1 and (440.21) K-word arcs, and zero-radius helices, throw ModelGapError. atan2/sin/hypot are double rounded once to float32, so a case exactly on a libm ulp boundary may differ. |
| LIM-HOLD-DWELL | both | Before EN 450.02, and on TG, a feedhold requested while a dwell runs in a moving cycle takes effect when the dwell ends (B-FH-1). |
| LIM-UNMODELLED | both | On 440.21 homing (G28.x); on edge-next G28.1/G28.4 (edge-next G28.2 and G28.3: LIM-EN-HOMING). G10 (except edge-next L2/L20, LIM-EN-G10), G28/G30, G43.1, G92.2/G92.3, G93, M105/M114/M115, M201.3, group SETs (except the edge-next sr list, LIM-EN-SR-LIST), baud/boot/defaults/test SETs throw ModelGapError. Use setHomed() for a homed machine. |
| LIM-EN-G10 | tinyg-en | Edge-next G10 L2 and L20 with P1..P6 set the G54..G59 offset and persist it, uncited (added for the Phase 2 fake board: set work zero). L20 uses the end of the last queued move as the current position; other L values are refused with status 130 as an unsupported command, other P values with P_WORD_IS_INVALID. 440.21 G10 still throws ModelGapError. |
| LIM-EN-SR-LIST | tinyg-en | Edge-next {"sr":{...}} replaces the status report list with the keys set to true, in order (TinyG report.c sr_set as remembered, uncited at the pin): a non-true value or unknown token is 100, an empty list 101, more than 30 entries 107 (INPUT_EXCEEDS_MAX_LENGTH, the closest status); it is persisted (one EEPROM write) and answered with the values of the new list. Kept in the EEPROM image as token indexes. |
| LIM-EN-SR-TIMING | tinyg-en | Status report requests are modelled as one timed request recorded at the first change against the values last sent; the report prints si ms later sampling the values then (report.c facts from the firmware maintainer, 2026-11-02, not cited at the pin). Which firmware events request a report is not modelled: any change of a listed value does. |
| LIM-EN-RT-HB | tinyg-en | The rt family as the single pair of a line: {"rt":null} reads hb, qt and up (whole seconds since power-up, runtime.c:179-185); {"rt":{"hb":N}} sets the RAM heartbeat in whole seconds, 0 off, 1..60 (RT_HB_MAX, runtime.h:6, :15); an integer above 60 or a negative is 110 and changes nothing, never clamped (runtime.c:107-118; util.c:224); a non-integer (1.5, a string) is 110 as the firmware maintainer stated (2026-11-02), though the typesafe parser read at 93a723b8 looks to answer 116 for those (json_parser.c:678-684; util.c:270), unverified on hardware (a JSON true is converted to 1 by that parser, json_parser.c:679-681; the model refuses it with 110); any other member 100; option rt:false answers 100. While hb > 0 a {"hb":{"stat","hold","up","qt"}} line prints every hb seconds while the link and the machine are quiet (JSON mode, no byte in or out, nothing unread; nothing moving, held, flushing or queued, runtime.c:33-93); any activity restarts the interval. hb is 0 after boot and ^X. Not modelled: qt (always ""), a beat skipped when it cannot go out whole, and the full planner-and-stepper quiet test (the model uses its motion queue). |
| LIM-EN-HOMING | tinyg-en | G28.2: each named axis needs exactly one homing switch (sn or sx mode 1 or 3), sv > 0 and am != 0, else the block fails with 246 (241 with no axis) and nothing moves. Axes home Z, X, Y, A as straight moves toward the switch end at sv mm/min (at most \|tm-tn\|+lb), then the axis position is set to tn or tm and marked homed; no latch, backoff or switch input is modelled. stat 9 while the cycle runs; a flush, an alarm, ^D or a reset ends it with the remaining axes unhomed. G28.3 queues a set of the named axes positions (unit-converted) and marks them homed. Uncited. |
| LIM-EN-RUNTIME-OFFSET | tinyg-en | A position report (pos, ofs) uses the work offset a move was queued with while a cycle runs or motion is running or held, and the model offset once both have stopped (_position_model, EN canonical_machine.c:2630-2636; plan_exec.c:216), so a G92, G10, G54..G59 or M2/M30 parsed ahead of running moves does not shift their work position. Not modelled: the queued offset command itself (_exec_offset, _exec_g10_offset, _exec_program_end): a change between two moves reaches the runtime with the next move, a cycle starts from the model offset until its first move runs, and the G53 zeroing applies to straight moves only. |
| LIM-EN-PRINT-UNITS | tinyg-en | While the model is in G20 the serializer prints F_CONVERT values in inches (prep_float, EN config_app.c:858-871, json_parser.c:828). Modelled for the coordinate offsets and stored positions g54..g59, g92, g28 and g30 on X, Y and Z only; the other F_CONVERT tokens (axis vm, fr, tn, tm, jm, jh, jd, sv, lv, lb, zb, the ra radii, ja, ct and the motor travel tr) still print in mm. |
| LIM-EN-PROBE | tinyg-en | Edge-next G38.2: the probe input has no 50 ms lockout and is sampled once per main-loop pass (1 ms); the stop after contact is the model hold (LIM-KINEMATICS), not a jerk-limited stop at zjh, so the overshoot is not the firmware stop distance; jerk and inverse-time mode are not modelled; the plate and lead are test controls (setProbePlate, setProbeTouch, setProbeLead); no status report is requested on a switch edge. |
| LIM-EN-RAM-WRITES | tinyg-en | Option ramWrites (default off) models a proposed firmware capability, not in any build: {"rt":{"unsaved":null}} answers unsaved 0, and a line whose first pair is ram:1 applies the rest in RAM without persisting. Without it any ram key answers 100 after the pairs before it have run. |
| LIM-TEXT | both | Text mode replies only with a prompt line; text-mode commands are not executed. |
| LIM-MESSAGES | both | Exception "msg" texts are the status names, not the firmware strings; (MSG ...) comments are ignored. |
| LIM-DEFAULTS | both | Settings defaults not marked with a settings file line are placeholders. |
| LIM-BOOT | both | Boot takes bootMs (default 1000 ms) before the banners; bytes received while booting are lost. |
| LIM-TX | both | No transmit-buffer backpressure on the main loop except the 440.21 host-XON stall; EN never blocks on TX (the E128 class on EN, B-KILL-2, is not modelled). |
| LIM-LINEPOOL | tinyg-en | Line-mode pool RAM is counted, not laid out: a new buffer needs more than 255 free bytes of the 1000. |
| LIM-FORCED-OVERRUN | link | A ringOverrun fault drops bytes even when the ring is not full; on EN a loss with an empty ring is reported at the reader at once. |
| LIM-BAUD | link | A baud-rate mismatch XORs every byte with 0xA5 instead of producing real framing errors. |
| LIM-TG-STATE-READS | tinyg-440 | The 440.21 connect-time state reads are modelled, uncited: home reads 1 when X, Y and Z are homed, tool reads 0, ofs is the active G54..G59 offset (the model has no G92), and the g92, g28 and g30 groups read 0. |
| LIM-TG-OVERLONG | tinyg-440 | Overlong lines on 440.21 throw ModelGapError. |
| LIM-REPORTS | both | Enumerated report values (momo, admo, frmo, macs, cycs, mots) use model numbering; qv=2 reports qr without qi/qo; status reports in text mode are still JSON. |
| LIM-MODAL-TG | tinyg-440 | Two codes of one modal group on a 440.21 line: the last one wins; no modal-group error is modelled. |
| LIM-EN-FEED-LIMIT | tinyg-en | The feed-limit push (option feedLimit, EN-FEED-LIMIT-PUSH) models the window, the interval and when fs lines are pushed; its counters do not model the firmware: ct is the time a cycle ran, cd is 0 and every per-cause counter in c is 0. Without feedLimitStep3 no fl lines are pushed; x is never set, and {"rt":{"fs":null}} is not modelled. |
| LIM-EN-FEED-LIMIT-STEP3 | tinyg-en | The optional c7f9b7e2 wire format is modelled separately from 450.02. Gap time/count uses the virtual model loop and motion-start evidence; no 250 ms coalescing, TX backpressure, transient underrun latch, counter wrap or fractional tick accounting. fs cause counters, fg boundary counters and fl executing-move causes stay zero/unknown. They must not validate physical attribution or performance. The job flag also works alone for capability tests; raw mixed rt group atomicity is not modelled. |
| LIM-EN-REPIN | tinyg-en | The model was built at edge-next ead63997; the 97321391, 6ec70652 and 93a723b8 re-pins (2026-11-02) and the a7489b79 re-pin (450.02, 2026-11-06) are modelled only for the spindle and coolant readouts spe, spc, spd, sps, cof and com (EN-SPINDLE-READOUTS; the model applies S when parsed, not queued, so sps follows a new S at once) and beyond that only as moved citations. Not modelled: the rt family beyond LIM-EN-RT-HB (at 93a723b8 the feed-limit report leaves flk, flm, flp and flf, the fl lines and the fs summary request, which the model answers 100 for; the push interval fi and its fs lines are modelled only with option feedLimit, EN-FEED-LIMIT-PUSH), E195 (a partial line quiet for about 1 s is dropped when a { arrives; the model always joins it to the next line), the stricter input errors E168-E177, E191 and E193, the timing fixes E165-E167, E180-E184, E190 and E192, and the planner fixes E196 (the junction limit read from the runtime direction when the previous block is freed) and E197 (a runtime halt clears the runtime exit velocity). For 450.02 and later the dwell planner-slot release and persisted-SET idle gate are modelled (EN-DWELL-IDLE). Other gaps from the 450.02 re-pin: fb 450.02 itself (the model reports 450.01 unless a caller passes build; the fake-serial board passes 450.02 so the committed bench manifest approves it), a feedhold while a cycle is stopped between moves entering HOLD at once (a feedhold during a dwell is modelled for a build of 450.02 or later, without the stale vel that hold reports), a queue flush or job kill also ending a dwell, status 118 after the banner for stored settings that would not load, the range-checked setters (axis rates, junction deviation, radius, chordal tolerance, ja, work offsets, PWM frequency), microsteps other than 1, 2, 4 and 8 refused, switch settings refused unless idle, targets above 1e18 refused, a resume whose held move cannot be replanned staying in HOLD with an exception, and the N66 hold endpoint fix. |
